chunks: A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
A man passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he was repairing one of his chambers. The man said: 'O Messenger of God, shall I not help you?' He said: 'As you wish.'

When he had finished, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What is your need?' He said: 'Paradise.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) fell silent, then said: 'Yes.'
When he turned to leave, he called to him: 'O servant of God, assist us by prolonging the prostration.'

key_terms.أَطْرَقَ: Fell silent with head bowed — a sign of deep contemplation or the gravity of what was being asked
key_terms.أَعِنَّا: Assist us — the Prophet's use of the plural 'us' here is notable, suggesting a spiritual partnership in worship
key_terms.السُّجُود: Prostration — the position in salat where one places the forehead on the ground, considered the moment of greatest closeness to God
key_terms.حُجُرَات: Chambers, private rooms — the Prophet's modest living quarters adjacent to the mosque
key_terms.شَأْنَكَ: As you wish / go ahead — an expression of consent and gracious acceptance of help

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about prolonging prostration (sajdah) as a means to paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an intimate encounter between the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and an anonymous man who helped repair the Prophet's chambers. When asked his need, the man simply asked for paradise, to which the Prophet first fell silent — suggesting deep consideration — then granted it, asking in return that the man assist 'us' (meaning himself and the man together) through prolonged prostration. The hadith emphasizes that salat, especially the act of prolonged sajdah, is a primary means of attaining paradise, and it reveals the Prophet's characteristic humility in manual labor and his generosity in granting intercession.
word_analysis: so he lowered his head/remained silent in contemplation

en.hubeali:
A group of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man passed by the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>saww</sup> was repairing one of his<sup>saww</sup> chambers, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Can I suffice (help) you<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If you so like’.
So when he was free, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘(What) is your need?’ He said, ‘The paradise’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> remained silent, then said: ‘Yes (Granted)’.
So when he turned around (to leave), hesaww said to him: ‘O servant of Allahazwj! Assist ussaww by prolonging Sajdah (the Zakāt)’’.
en.sarwar: 8. A group of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a man passed by the Holy Prophet while he was doing some work around one of his rooms. He asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, can I help you?’ He (the Holy Prophet) replied, ‘If you like, you may do so.’

When the work finished the Messenger of Allah asked, ’Can I do anything for you?’ ’Paradise, 5 the man pleaded. The Messenger of Allah looked into the sky then said, ‘Yes, (paradise is your reward). 5
When he was leaving the Messenger of Allah said, ‘O servant of Allah, you must assist us by prolonging your Sajdah.
